transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Nina Ortega (Redwood CSM), Sarah Morales (Lyceum CISO), Jason Park (Eng Manager), Leila Hassan (DevOps), Michael Trent (Legal), Tommy (intern)

(auto-generated topics:) Audit capture, export destinations, KMS residency, retention & legal hold, SOC2 evidence

00:00 Priya Shah: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh we're from Redwood, I'm Priya, AE on the account. Quick agenda to make sure we cover what Lyceum needs for admin events and long term archives.
00:18 Sarah Morales: Thanks Priya, quick note, I'm Sarah, CISO. Primary ask is: we need a defensible audit trail for admin actions and logins, retention for seven years for some cohorts, and proof for SOC2/ISO audits.
00:31 Priya Shah: Got it. Ethan and I will walk through what we capture today, export options, and where KMS fits in.
00:40 Ethan Liu: Cool, so quick top-level: Redwood captures control-plane events and admin activity, things like user creation/deletion, role changes, API key ops, SSO logins, session failures, token revocations, model deployment changes, and admin console actions. We also capture system-level events — schedulers, autoscale events — though those are lower fidelity for now.
01:05 Jason Park: When you say SSO logins, do you capture both successful and failed auth attempts? We need both for our detection rules.
01:12 Ethan Liu: Yes both. We timestamp, user principal, origin IP, and approximate device metadata when available. Note: some fields may be redacted for privacy if the policy is enabled.
01:22 Sarah Morales: And RBAC change history? Like full before/after diffs?
01:28 Ethan Liu: We capture the event and the effected principal and the role change. Full diffs — we include the snapshot of roles and role bindings at the time, but there's occasional truncation for very large policy objects. We recommend exporting raw events to your SIEM for deep forensic diffs.
01:45 Leila Hassan: Are these events stored in your control plane or in the customer VPC for private deployments? Our policy prefers not storing PII in vendor control planes for anything older than 90 days.
01:55 Priya Shah: Good callout. For Hosted Redwood, default control plane stores events for 90 days in our telemetry store. For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) you can opt for local event ingestion where events land in your VPC S3 or a configured Kafka. For the Private option events can be sent only to your KMS-protected bucket, redwood doesn't retain copies.
02:18 Michael Trent: Legal — is that documented as an option and do you provide attestations that vendor doesn't keep backups?
02:25 Nina Ortega: We have a signed addendum for Private deployments where retention in Redwood control plane is turned off; I'll attach the template.
02:33 Priya Shah: I'll include the addendum and the SOC2/ISO artifacts in the follow-up.
02:40 Tommy (intern): sorry quick dumb q, is KV cache events also included?
02:46 Ethan Liu: Ha, KV cache, yes — we capture cache-warm events and cache-evicts in the operational telemetry bucket; not all of that is surfaced in the default admin-audit feed but it's available via export hooks for performance forensics.
03:03 Jason Park: Exporting — what are the destinations and protocols? We run Splunk and also a Kafka cluster.
03:10 Ethan Liu: Supported targets: S3 (CSV/JSON), stream to Kafka (Avro/JSON), streaming webhooks (for SIEMs), and direct syslog/Fluentd connector examples. We also have a managed forwarder to Splunk HTTP Event Collector. For higher throughput we suggest Kafka with Avro schemas.
03:29 Sarah Morales: Encryption — we have strict KMS requirements: customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS, HSM-backed keys for legal hold. Do you support bringing our CMK?
03:39 Ethan Liu: Yes, for Private and Dedicated you can bring your CMK; for Hosted we support envelope encryption where you can supply a wrapped-encryption-key via BYOK flows — practically, we support customer-managed KMS via cross-account grants and your CMK can encrypt S3 archives. HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM) can be integrated in the Private offering.
03:57 Michael Trent: Is there an audit trail for the key use? We need to show key access events to auditors.
04:04 Ethan Liu: We emit KMS operation logs as part of the export feed where available, and you can also pull CloudTrail logs from your account for Private deployments. In Hosted there's an access log we can provide as part of the evidence pack but the canonical key usage logs in Hosted are limited by the KMS provider.
04:25 Leila Hassan: Retention policies — default 90 days in-hosted, but we'd like seven-year WORM for certain admin exports.
04:33 Priya Shah: Two-tier approach: short-term (90 days) in Redwood for quick lookup and observability; long-term archival you export to your S3 archive which you can set to WORM/GLACIER and lifecycle rules to 7 years. We can configure a legal-hold flag that pins objects from deletion on export.
04:52 Sarah Morales: For compliance evidence we also need tamper-evidence and checksum chain. Does Redwood sign or provide SHA checksums of exports?
04:59 Ethan Liu: Yes, for every exported archive we include SHA256 manifests and a signed manifest file. For Private deployments where the object never touches Redwood's control plane we provide a signed receipt and manifest from the agent that writes the object.
05:16 Jason Park: What about indexing and search? If we keep everything in S3, how do we do quick queries during an investigation?
05:23 Ethan Liu: You can stream to Elasticsearch/Opensearch in parallel for hot indexing. Or use Athena/Glue over partitioned JSON/Parquet exports. We publish a recommended partitioning scheme in the export playbook.
05:36 Sarah Morales: Data residency: Lyceum processes EU patient metadata; we need events for EU objects to stay in EU.
:05:44 Priya Shah: For region pinning we support tenant-level region residency: events originating from EU regions can be routed to EU-only export endpoints and EU-only storage in both Dedicated and Hosted tier, though Hosted has additional controls and cross-border replication requires opt-in. For strict policy we recommend Private (VPC) in EU region.
06:03 Leila Hassan: Are you able to filter what gets exported? We only want admin events and SSO, not low-level telemetry for performance by default.
06:11 Ethan Liu: Yes you can configure export filters by event-type, by principal, and by resource type. We'll share our event taxonomy — but quick note: some derived events (autoscale, infra heartbeats) are only in operational telemetry not admin-audit by default.
06:25 Jason Park: How does signature verification work on restore? If auditors pull an object from S3 years later, how can they prove it's untouched?
06:33 Ethan Liu: The signed manifest contains object checksums and signer metadata; for Hosted we sign with Redwood's service key and include a chain of trust. For Private we recommend you sign with your CMK and we provide the agent-signed receipt.
06:46 Sarah Morales: For legal holds — can Redwood apply holds on objects we export? E.g., if we request a hold on a set of user events for an ongoing investigation.
06:55 Priya Shah: Two options: you can set legal hold in your archive bucket (recommended), or we can set a surrogate hold in Redwood control plane for the 90-day window and flag subsequent exports as under hold in the manifest. For long holds we don't recommend relying on Redwood control plane alone.
07:16 Michael Trent: Does your addendum mention subpoena support or eDiscovery workflows?
07:21 Nina Ortega: We'll attach a process doc — but legal requests must flow through our legal ops and we can provide exports per the contract. For Private deployments, since data is in your VPC, eDiscovery is handled by your process.
07:33 Tommy (intern): sorry again, what's the difference between dedicated and private here?
07:38 Priya Shah: Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware reserved for you (no multi-tenant sharing at runtime) but control plane still lives with Redwood unless configured otherwise; Private pulls the control plane into your VPC or on-prem with options to disable Redwood storage entirely.
07:53 Jason Park: Are there cost implications of long-term retention? We need a ballpark for 7-year retention of x TB archived annually.
08:01 Priya Shah: Costs: Redwood charges for export egress and optionally for managed archival routing. For Private, if objects stay in your S3, Redwood charges are lower (mainly for agent telemetry), but you'll pay your storage and lifecycle costs. We'll provide a cost estimate spreadsheet with sample retention scenarios.
08:17 Sarah Morales: Evidence and audits — can you produce a consolidated evidence pack for SOC2 with admin events and KMS proof?
08:24 Ethan Liu: Yes, that's our evidence pack. It includes event samples, manifests, key-use logs, role-change snapshots, and the signed manifests. For ISO we include the same artifacts plus our policy documents. We'll send redacted examples.
08:36 Leila Hassan: For the POC we want to try: 1) export admin events for the last 30 days to our EU S3 bucket, 2) stream a subset (RBAC changes + auth failures) into our Kafka cluster, and 3) verify manifest signatures.
08:52 Priya Shah: Sounds good. Proposed POC acceptance criteria: successful export of 30 days of events to EU S3 with SHA256 manifests; streaming throughput >= 500 eps; manifest validation script runs and verifies signatures.
09:10 Jason Park: About signatures — can we use our own signing key (outside KMS)? We have an HSM in-house.
09:17 Ethan Liu: Yes — the agent can produce signed manifests with your private key, or you can sign post-export. We'll provide hooks in the export pipeline to call your signing service in the VPC.
09:28 Sarah Morales: Any blockers for retention compliance? We need chain-of-custody documentation for each exported object.
09:35 Priya Shah: We'll include chain-of-custody metadata in the manifest (timestamp, uploader agent id, uploader hostname, checksum, and optional KMS key-id). For Hosted maybe some fields are Redwood-managed, but we will document each field.
09:52 Michael Trent: On discovery requests, what's the timeline for Redwood to produce an ad-hoc export?
09:58 Nina Ortega: Standard SLA is 48 hours for hosted evidence requests; for Private it's within your infra timeframes. We can negotiate faster SLAs in the contract.
10:08 Jason Park: Are there alerts for unexpected admin activity (e.g., mass role deletions)?
10:13 Ethan Liu: Yes, Redwood Console supports rule-based alerts and automatic snapshot exports on trigger events. You can set canary exports that snapshot the involved objects.
10:24 Leila Hassan: How do you handle PII redaction in exports? We want to strip user email domains when exporting to non-prod.
10:32 Ethan Liu: Export pipeline supports field transforms including regex redaction. We can configure transforms per export target and maintain a redaction policy.
10:41 Sarah Morales: For the auditors, can you map events to control IDs? E.g., map the role-change event to CC5.3 in our control matrix.
10:49 Priya Shah: Yep, we can include control mapping metadata. We often include a control-id mapping in the evidence pack as a CSV.
10:57 Michael Trent: Any vendors you're integrated with for long-term immutable storage? We use an archival partner for legal hold.
11:03 Ethan Liu: Any S3-compatible bucket works; we support signed URLs, putObject with manifest, and multipart. If you have a partner, we can route to them through S3 or via our connector.
11:12 Jason Park: One last question: do we get user-level audit logs for API keys — like which key triggered which model run?
11:19 Ethan Liu: Yes, every request has a token-id and you can map token-id to owner in the token registry export. We capture model-run metadata (model id, seq length, latency).
11:30 Priya Shah: Okay let's recap action items and next steps.
11:35 Priya Shah: (recap) Priya will send SOC2 and the audit export playbook, Ethan will provide connector configs and a small perf benchmark, Nina will attach the addendum template, Leila will confirm residency requirements, and we'll schedule the POC for next Tuesday.
11:55 Sarah Morales: Great, thanks everyone. Anything else from legal?
12:00 Michael Trent: No, we'll review the addendum and follow up with redlines.
12:05 Priya Shah: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links.

References mentioned: https://redwood.ai/docs/export-playbook (internal link), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (artifact), shared drive: /lyceum-security/evidence-pack

(End of transcript)
